title.narrative: Reviving Le Grand Théâtre de Beyrouth

description.narrative: Le Grand Théâtre de Beyrouth, inaugurated in 1929 and designed by the visionary architect Youssef Aftimos, once embodied Beirut’s cosmopolitan spirit. Through the mid-20th century, the venue was a vibrant epicenter of Arab and international performance arts, welcoming legendary performers such as Oum Kalthoum, Mohamed Abdel Wahab, and the Comédie Française. It played a pivotal role in shaping Lebanon's cultural renaissance. Tragically, since the outbreak of the Lebanese Civil War in 1975 and its official closure in 1990, the theatre has stood in silence. Officially closed in 1990, the theatre still stands behind a façade partially restored by Solidere in 1994, while its interior remains in poor condition. When protesters briefly reclaimed the building during the October 2019 revolution, their impromptu performances underlined both the public’s attachment to this landmark and the hunger of Lebanese youth for a civic stage. Following the 2020 Beirut-Port explosion, the city was exposed to a deeper deficit - a lack of inclusive cultural infrastructure. Today, existing performance halls are few, often privately run, and inaccessible to large segments of society. In the heart of downtown Beirut, the Grand Théâtre, historically a gathering place for cultural events, political demonstrations and everyday urban life. now sits unused at a moment when Lebanon faces social fragmentation and economic difficulties. Its restoration is therefore not merely a conservation project, but it is a social and economic imperative. UNESCO, in cooperation with the Ministry of Culture and Solidere (the theatre’s owner), proposes to rehabilitate the venue and establish a legal and governance framework that combines public oversight with private-sector expertise, with a view reopen the Grand Théâtre. Preliminary talks with the Minister of Culture are already under way. Before physical restoration can begin, a comprehensive series of studies must be conducted to assess its current state, legal standing, cultural value, and future viability—laying the foundation for a safe, sustainable, and meaningful rehabilitation - that will constitute the phase 1 of this project.
